mainTopic: Which days get full הלל, and the instruments and vessels of the מקדש
overview: The גמרא explains which days get the full הלל. Every day of סוכות has different offerings, so each day gets הלל, while the days of פסח are all the same. Testing this, it adds that the day must be called a מועד (which rules out שבת) and must have work forbidden (which rules out ראש חודש). ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים pass every test but are left out, because רבי אבהו teaches that joyful song does not fit a day of judgment. חנוכה gets הלל for its miracle, and the גמרא gives three answers for why פורים does not: the miracle was outside ארץ ישראל, the מגילה reading is its הלל, or we were still servants of אחשורוש. Then it returns to the משנה's flute and explains that חליל and אבוב are one instrument. A ברייתא tells how the old reed flute, copper cymbal and copper mortar of the מקדש worked worse when changed or repaired, and how the שילוח spring gave less water when widened. The amud ends with teachings about instruments in the מקדש: the הרדולים, which was not used, and the מגריפה, whose description continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why every day of סוכות but not every day of פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a question that began earlier: why is full הלל said every day of סוכות but not every day of פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: [Why do we say full הלל on] every day [of סוכות, but not on every day of פסח]?
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish a question that started on the previous amud. The question is why full הלל is said on all the days of סוכות but not on all the days of פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both סוכות and פסח are multi-day festivals, so we would expect them to be treated the same. The question asks what makes סוכות different. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The special praise made of תהלים 113–118, said on festive days

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a full question on its own. It is only the end of a question that began earlier, so you need the start of it to make sense of it.

phrases.english: every day?
phrases.notes: This finishes the question: why do we say full הלל every day of סוכות, but not every day of פסח?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the question that started before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason full הלל is said every day of סוכות but not every day of פסח?

steps.title: The days of סוכות have different offerings; the days of פסח do not
steps.stepSummary: Each day of סוכות has its own set of offerings, so each day counts as a new festive day. The days of פסח all have the same offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because on סוכות the days are different from each other in their offerings, but on פסח the days are not different from each other in their offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Every day of סוכות has different מוסף offerings, so each day gets its own full הלל. The days of פסח all have the same offerings, so full הלל is said only at the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule here is that a day which is unique in its offerings counts as its own festive day and gets full הלל. On סוכות the number of bulls changes every day, so every day is new. On פסח the later days only repeat the first day, so they do not get a separate full הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Their offerings (here, the מוסף offerings of each day)
Here it means the festival of סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the first test for full הלל: is the day unique in its offerings? The rest of the section checks whether this test is enough on its own.

phrases.english: Because on the festival [of סוכות], the days are different in their offerings,
but on פסח the days are not different in their offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A day that is different in its offerings gets its own full הלל. Every day of סוכות is different; the days of פסח are not.

steps.title: Challenge: שבת has its own offerings, so say הלל
steps.stepSummary: If different offerings are the reason for הלל, then שבת, which has its own special offerings, should get הלל too.
steps.simpleTranslation: שבת is different in its offerings, so let us say [הלל on it]!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer it just gave. שבת has its own מוסף offering, so by that reasoning we should say הלל on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'different offerings' were the whole reason, שבת should qualify. Since we do not say הלל on שבת, there must be another condition as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (here: let us say הלל)
The weekly day of rest, which has its own מוסף offering

phrases.english: שבת, which is different in its offerings,
let us say [הלל]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a day with different offerings gets הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבת has different offerings, yet no הלל is said on it, so the rule is not enough.

steps.title: שבת is not called a מועד
steps.stepSummary: שבת does not get הלל because the תורה does not call it a מועד, an appointed festive time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not called a 'מועד'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a day must also be called a מועד in the תורה to get הלל. שבת is not called a מועד, so it does not get הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a second condition: the day must be a מועד, a festival. Different offerings alone are not enough. שבת fails this second test.

keyTerms.meaning: An appointed festive time, as the תורה calls the festivals

phrases.english: It is not called a 'מועד'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 3 by adding a condition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Different offerings alone are enough for הלל, so שבת should qualify.
steps.terutzMaskana: The day must also be called a מועד, and שבת is not.

steps.title: Challenge: ראש חודש is called a מועד, so say הלל
steps.stepSummary: ראש חודש has its own offerings and is called a מועד, so it seems it should get full הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: ראש חודש is called a 'מועד', so let us say [הלל on it]!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new condition. ראש חודש is called a מועד and has its own offerings, so it seems to pass both tests and should get full הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two conditions now in place, ראש חודש seems to meet both. Since full הלל is not required on it, there must be a third condition.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the Jewish month, which has its own מוסף offering

phrases.english: ראש חודש, which is called a 'מועד',
let us say [הלל]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 4 with a new case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two conditions: different offerings and being called a מועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ראש חודש meets both conditions, yet full הלל is not required on it.

steps.title: ראש חודש is not made holy by forbidding work
steps.stepSummary: ראש חודש does not get full הלל because work is not forbidden on it. A פסוק shows that only a day made holy as a festival needs song.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not made holy by forbidding work, as it is written: 'You shall have a song as on the night when a festival is made holy.' A night that is made holy as a festival needs song; one that is not made holy as a festival does not need song.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a day also has to be holy in the sense that work is forbidden on it. Work is allowed on ראש חודש, so it does not get full הלל. A פסוק from ישעיהו supports this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a third condition: the day must be holy, with work forbidden. The פסוק links song (הלל) to a day that is 'made holy as a festival'. Since ראש חודש is not made holy that way, it does not need song.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing work (the kind forbidden on a festival)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the full הלל is not required on ראש חודש. The partial הלל said today on ראש חודש is a custom, not this requirement.

phrases.english: It is not made holy by [forbidding] the doing of work,
as it is written: 'You shall have a song
as on the night when a festival is made holy' —
a night that is made holy as a festival needs song,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵין מְקוּדָּשׁ לֶחָג אֵין טָעוּן שִׁירָה.
phrases.english: and one that is not made holy as a festival does not need song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 5 by adding a third condition and giving a פסוק for it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a needed condition, backed by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being a מועד with different offerings is enough, so ראש חודש should get full הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The day must also be holy with work forbidden, and ראש חודש is not.

steps.title: Challenge: ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים pass every test
steps.stepSummary: ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים are called a מועד and work is forbidden on them, so they should get הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים are called a 'מועד' and are made holy by forbidding work, so let us say [הלל on them]!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two days that seem to meet every condition so far. They are called a מועד, work is forbidden, and they have their own offerings, yet we do not say הלל on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three conditions from steps 2, 4 and 6 seem to apply to these days. So the conditions alone cannot explain why הלל is not said. Some other reason must be at work.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year, the Day of Judgment

phrases.english: ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים,
which are called a 'מועד',
and are made holy by [forbidding] the doing of work,
let us say [הלל]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the full set of conditions built up in steps 2–6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The three conditions for saying הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים meet every condition, yet הלל is not said on them.

steps.title: Because of the teaching of רבי אבהו
steps.stepSummary: הלל is not said on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים because of a teaching of רבי אבהו, which the גמרא will quote next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of [the teaching] of רבי אבהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to a teaching of רבי אבהו. It is setting up the next move, where it will quote that teaching and explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These days do qualify under the three conditions. They are still left out for a different reason, which comes from רבי אבהו's teaching. This is a special exception, not a claim that these days are not festivals.
steps.whatToRemember: Full הלל needs a day with its own offerings, called a מועד, and made holy with work forbidden. ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים are a special exception because of רבי אבהו's teaching.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים fail to be real festivals. They meet every condition; they are left out only because of a separate reason that comes next.

phrases.english: Because of [the teaching] of רבי אבהו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 7 by pointing to a separate teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an outside reason for the exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since these days meet all the conditions, הלל should be said on them.
steps.terutzMaskana: A separate teaching of רבי אבהו explains why הלל is not said on them.

steps.title: Days of judgment are not a time for joyful song
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא told the angels that a joyful song does not fit while the books of life and death lie open before Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבהו said: The angels asked ה׳, 'Master of the world, why don't the Jewish people sing praise to You on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים?' He answered: 'Is it possible? The King sits on the throne of judgment, and the books of life and the books of death are open before Him, and the Jewish people should sing songs to Me?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the teaching of רבי אבהו that it promised in the last step. This teaching explains why ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים have no הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These days meet both earlier conditions: they are called a מועד, and work is forbidden on them. Even so, the mood of the day blocks הלל. Everyone is being judged, and a joyful song does not fit a day of judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: Song of praise; here it means הלל
The books of life and the books of death, where each person's judgment is written

steps.whyThisMatters: This adds a new idea to the rules about הלל. A day can qualify on paper, but if it is a day of fear and judgment, joyful הלל is not said.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Abbahu said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה לְפָנֶיךָ
phrases.english: for what reason do the Jewish people not say song before You
on Rosh HaShana and on Yom Kippur?
He said to them: Is it possible
that the King is sitting on the throne of judgment,
and the books of life and the books of death
are open before Him,
and the Jewish people would say song before Me?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the רבי אבהו teaching that step 8 pointed to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Days of judgment do not get הלל, because joyful song does not fit while life and death are being decided.

steps.title: Challenge from חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: חנוכה has no special offering and no ban on work, yet הלל is said on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about חנוכה? It has neither this nor that, and still we say הלל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rules it built up. חנוכה fails both conditions, yet we say הלל on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps tied הלל to two things: being a מועד with its own offerings, and having work forbidden. חנוכה has neither of these. So why does it get הלל?

keyTerms.meaning: The eight-day holiday from the time of the חשמונאים

phrases.english: But there is Hanukkah,
which has neither this nor that,
phrases.notes: "This" and "that" are the two conditions from before: a special offering, and a ban on work.

phrases.english: and yet one says it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא חֲנוּכָּה דְּלָא הָכִי וְלָא הָכִי, וְקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים, the גמרא tests the rules against a holiday from the other direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that הלל depends on a day having its own offerings and having work forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנוכה meets neither condition, yet has הלל, so the rules seem incomplete.

steps.title: חנוכה's הלל is for the miracle
steps.stepSummary: On חנוכה, הלל is said because of the miracle, not because the day is a festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of the miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in a few words. חנוכה gets הלל for a different reason, the miracle that happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two separate reasons to say הלל. One is the holiness of a festival day. The other is thanks for a miracle. חנוכה falls under the second reason.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the earlier rules. A festival is still a reason for הלל; a miracle is simply a second, separate reason.

phrases.english: Because of the miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from חנוכה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a second, separate reason for הלל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הלל comes only from festival status.
steps.terutzMaskana: A miracle is also a reason to say הלל.

steps.title: Then why not פורים?
steps.stepSummary: פורים also had a miracle, so it should get הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: פורים also has a miracle, so let us say הלל on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the new answer to raise a new problem. If a miracle is enough for הלל, פורים should have it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer about חנוכה seems to prove too much. פורים also celebrates a great miracle, yet no הלל is said on it.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiday celebrating the rescue in the days of אחשורוש

phrases.english: Purim, where there is a miracle,
let one say it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from step 11 to attack from a new angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a miracle brings הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פורים had a miracle but has no הלל, which goes against the rule.

steps.title: No song for a miracle outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the פורים miracle happened outside ארץ ישראל, and we do not sing שירה for such a miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Because we do not say song for a miracle that happened outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers why פורים has no הלל. Its miracle happened in Persia, outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a limit to the miracle reason. Only a miracle that happened in ארץ ישראל calls for הלל. The miracle of חנוכה happened in ארץ ישראל, so it qualifies; פורים does not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
Because one does not say song
for a miracle that happened outside the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה עַל נֵס שֶׁבְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פורים challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule to miracles in ארץ ישראל
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a miracle in ארץ ישראל brings הלל.

steps.title: Challenge from the Exodus
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק points out that יציאת מצרים happened outside ארץ ישראל, yet we say הלל for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק objected: But יציאת מצרים was a miracle outside ארץ ישראל, and we say הלל for it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks רבי יצחק's answer. He brings the biggest miracle of all, which happened in Egypt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we never sing for a miracle outside ארץ ישראל, we should not say הלל for leaving Egypt. But we clearly do say it, on פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (raised a strong objection)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak objected to this:
But there is the Exodus from Egypt,
which is a miracle outside the Land,
and we say Hallel!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: וַהֲרֵי יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of רבי יצחק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that there is no song for a miracle outside ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יציאת מצרים happened outside ארץ ישראל, yet we say הלל for it.

steps.title: Before entering ארץ ישראל, every land counted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that before the Jews entered ארץ ישראל, a miracle in any land called for שירה. After they entered, only ארץ ישראל does.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Before the Jews entered ארץ ישראל, all lands were fit for saying song. Once they entered the Land, the other lands were no longer fit for saying song.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יצחק with a ברייתא. The rule about outside the Land only started once the Jews entered ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יציאת מצרים happened before the Jews entered the Land, when every land was still fit for שירה. The פורים miracle came after they entered, so a miracle outside the Land no longer calls for song.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Until the Jewish people entered the Land,
all the lands were fit for saying song;
once they entered the Land,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הוּכְשְׁרוּ כׇּל אֲרָצוֹת לוֹמַר שִׁירָה.
phrases.english: all the other lands were no longer fit for saying song.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנְסוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from יציאת מצרים and saves רבי יצחק's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a line in time, using a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule about outside the Land has always applied.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only began once the Jews entered ארץ ישראל, so יציאת מצרים is not a problem.

steps.title: Reading the מגילה is the הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives another answer: on פורים, reading the מגילה takes the place of הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Its reading is its הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a different answer to why פורים has no הלל. Reading the מגילה already does the job of הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן agrees that the פורים miracle does call for praise. That praise is given through reading the מגילה, so a separate הלל is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Its reading; here, reading the מגילה

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Its reading is its Hallel.
phrases.notes: "Its reading" means reading מגילת אסתר on פורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: קְרִיָּיתָהּ זוֹ הִיא הַלֵּילָאּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פורים question from step 12 and offers a second answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Something else takes the place of הלל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פורים seems to have no praise at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מגילה reading is פורים's praise.

steps.title: We are still servants of אחשורוש
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a third answer: הלל calls us 'servants of ה׳' and no one else's, but after פורים we were still under אחשורוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It makes sense there, at יציאת מצרים, to say 'Give praise, servants of ה׳,' and not servants of פרעה. But here, can we say 'Give praise, servants of ה׳,' and not servants of אחשורוש? We are still servants of אחשורוש!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third answer about פורים. The words of הלל themselves do not fit the situation after the פורים miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל opens with 'Give praise, servants of ה׳,' which means we serve only ה׳. After leaving Egypt that was true, because we were free of פרעה. After פורים the Jews stayed in exile under Persian rule, so those words would not be honest.

keyTerms.meaning: "Give praise, servants of ה׳", the opening of הלל

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers for why פורים has no הלל. רבי יצחק: the miracle happened outside ארץ ישראל. רב נחמן: the מגילה reading is the הלל. רבא: we were still servants of אחשורוש.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Granted, there one can say: "Give praise, servants of the Lord,"
phrases.notes: "There" means יציאת מצרים. The פסוק is תהלים 113:1.

phrases.english: and not servants of Pharaoh;
but here, can one say "Give praise, servants of the Lord,"
and not servants of Ahasuerus?
We are still servants of Ahasuerus!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם ״הַלְלוּ עַבְדֵי ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to the פורים question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out that the words of הלל do not fit פורים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any miracle of rescue fits the words of הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: הלל fits only a full rescue to freedom, and פורים left the Jews under foreign rule.

steps.title: How can רב נחמן count the מגילה as הלל for a miracle outside the Land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן: the ברייתא says that after entering ארץ ישראל, miracles in other lands no longer call for שירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב נחמן, who said the reading of the מגילה is its הלל: doesn't the ברייתא teach that once the Jews entered the Land, all other lands were no longer fit for saying שירה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's answer from step 16 using the ברייתא from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said the מגילה reading is a kind of הלל. But the ברייתא says that after entering ארץ ישראל, we sing no שירה for a miracle in another land. The פורים miracle happened in פרס, so how can any form of הלל be said for it?

keyTerms.meaning: Its reading (the reading of the מגילה)
Its הלל, its song of praise
They were no longer fit or suitable
Song of praise to ה׳ for a miracle

phrases.english: And according to Rav Nachman, who said:
phrases.notes: This goes back to his answer in step 16.

phrases.english: its reading is itself its hallel,
but isn't it taught in a baraita:
once they entered the Land,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הוּכְשְׁרוּ כׇּל אֲרָצוֹת לוֹמַר שִׁירָה,
phrases.english: all the other lands were no longer fit for saying song?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב נַחְמָן דְּאָמַר קְרִיָּיתָהּ זוֹ הִיא הַלֵּילָא הָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב נחמן's answer in step 16 and tests it against the ברייתא in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that reading the מגילה counts as הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says miracles outside ארץ ישראל no longer call for שירה after the Jews entered the Land, and the פורים miracle happened outside the Land.

steps.title: After the exile, other lands went back to their original status
steps.stepSummary: Once the Jews were exiled, the other lands again became fit for שירה, so the מגילה can serve as הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they were exiled, the lands returned to their original permitted status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן: the ברייתא's rule only applied while the Jews lived in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that only ארץ ישראל calls for שירה was limited to the time the Jews lived there. After the exile, other lands went back to the way they were before the Jews entered the Land. The פורים miracle happened after the exile, so a kind of הלל (the מגילה) fits.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean we say the regular הלל on פורים. For רב נחמן, the reading of the מגילה itself is the הלל.

phrases.english: Once they were exiled,
the lands returned to their original permitted status.
phrases.notes: He means the status from before the Jews entered the Land, when a miracle anywhere called for שירה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא's rule to the time the Jews lived in ארץ ישראל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the Jews entered ארץ ישראל, other lands lost their fitness for שירה forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the exile, other lands went back to their old status, so the פורים miracle can be praised with the מגילה as its הלל.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers for why we don't say הלל on פורים: the miracle was outside the Land (רבי יצחק), the מגילה is the הלל (רב נחמן), and we were still servants of אחשורוש (רבא). רב נחמן holds that after the exile, other lands went back to being fit for שירה.

steps.title: Why does the משנה switch from חליל to אבוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about not playing a copper flute and asks why it opens with the word חליל and ends with אבוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'He would not play on a copper אבוב, etc.' The משנה opens with the word חליל and ends with the word אבוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and points out that it uses two different words for the flute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה first talks about the חליל and then says the musician would not play an אבוב of copper. Two different words make it look like two different instruments, so the גמרא asks what is going on.

keyTerms.meaning: It opens with ... and ends with (pointing out a change in wording)

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה מַכֶּה בְּאַבּוּב שֶׁל נְחוֹשֶׁת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: The משנה said: He would not play on a copper abuv, etc.
It opens with 'chalil'
and ends with 'abuv'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the פורים discussion and returns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה use two different names, and are they two different instruments?

steps.title: חליל and אבוב are the same instrument
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that חליל and אבוב are one instrument. It is called חליל because its sound is sweet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A חליל is the same as an אבוב. Why is it called a חליל? Because its sound is sweet.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: there is only one instrument here with two names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not talking about two instruments. אבוב is the instrument's name, and חליל is a nickname based on the word for 'sweet' (חלי), because its sound is pleasant.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as that

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
a chalil is the same as an abuv,
and why is it called 'chalil'?
Because its sound is sweet.
phrases.notes: A play on words: חליל sounds like חלי, 'sweet'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא הַיְינוּ חָלִיל הַיְינוּ אַבּוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two words name one instrument. חליל is a descriptive name meaning 'sweet-sounding'.

steps.title: The reed flute lost its sweet sound when plated with gold
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes an old reed flute in the מקדש. The king had it plated with gold, its sound got worse, and removing the plating brought the sound back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There was a flute in the מקדש. It was smooth, thin, made of reed, and from the days of משה. The king ordered it plated with gold, and its sound was no longer pleasant. They removed the plating, and its sound was pleasant as before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that fits the משנה's point that the reed flute, not a metal one, had the pleasing sound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the flute fancier with gold actually ruined its sound. Only the plain reed in its original form sounded right. This matches the משנה, which preferred a reed flute over a copper one.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught in a baraita:
There was a flute in the Temple;
it was smooth, it was thin,
it was made of reed,
and it was from the days of Moshe.
The king commanded, and they plated it with gold,
and its sound was not pleasant;
they removed its plating,
and its sound was pleasant as it had been.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the משנה's flute with a related ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The original reed flute sounded best. Plating it with gold spoiled its sound.

steps.title: The repaired copper cymbal lost its sweet sound
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a copper cymbal in the מקדש was damaged and fixed by craftsmen from Alexandria. The repair spoiled its sound, and removing the repair brought the sound back.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a copper cymbal in the מקדש with a pleasant sound. It got damaged, and the חכמים brought craftsmen from Alexandria in Egypt who fixed it. Its sound was no longer pleasant. They removed the repair, and its sound was pleasant as before.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second example of the same pattern, this time with a copper cymbal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even skilled experts could not improve on the original. Their repair made things worse, and only removing it brought the cymbal back to its proper sound.

phrases.english: There was a cymbal in the Temple;
it was made of copper,
and its sound was pleasant, and it became damaged,
and the Sages sent for and brought craftsmen
from Alexandria of Egypt, and they repaired it,
and its sound was not pleasant;
they removed its repair,
and its sound was pleasant as it had been.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The repaired cymbal sounded worse. Removing the repair brought back its original sound.

steps.title: The repaired copper mortar stopped grinding the spices well
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's third example: a copper mortar from the days of משה, used to grind the spices, was damaged and repaired. It stopped working well until the repair was removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a copper mortar in the מקדש from the days of משה, used to grind the spices. It got damaged, and craftsmen from Alexandria in Egypt fixed it. It no longer ground the spices as well as before. They removed the repair, and it ground them as well as it used to.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a third example of the same pattern, a vessel that worked best in its original form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the vessel is not a musical instrument but the mortar for the spices. The lesson is the same: a repair from outside could not match the original, and taking it out restored the vessel's proper function.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives three examples (the reed flute, the copper cymbal and the copper mortar). In each one, changing or repairing the original vessel of the מקדש made it worse, and removing the change brought it back to how it was.

phrases.english: There was a mortar in the Temple;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל נְחוֹשֶׁת הָיְתָה, וּמִימוֹת מֹשֶׁה הָיְתָה,
phrases.english: it was made of copper, and it was from the days of Moshe,
and it would grind and blend the spices.
It became damaged, and they brought craftsmen
from Alexandria of Egypt, and they repaired it,
and it did not grind as well as it had before;
they removed its repair,
and it ground as well as it had before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and last example in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The repaired mortar worked worse. Removing the repair restored its original function.

steps.title: The two copper vessels were left over from the first Temple
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying the cymbal and the mortar came from the מקדש ראשון. It connects them to פסוקים that praise their special copper.
steps.simpleTranslation: These two vessels were left over from the first מקדש. They got damaged and could not be properly fixed. דוד described them as 'burnished copper' and 'polished copper,' and the פסוק in עזרא calls them 'vessels of fine golden copper, two, precious as gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list by explaining where the cymbal and the mortar came from and quoting פסוקים that describe them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why no craftsman could repair them: they were unique vessels from the מקדש ראשון, made of a special copper. The פסוקים show that this copper was so fine it was compared to gold. The words 'two, precious as gold' set up the next discussion about what exactly this comparison means.

keyTerms.meaning: got damaged, became chipped or cracked
burnished / polished, meaning shiny and refined

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ שְׁנֵי כֵלִים נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ מִמִּקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: These two vessels were left over from the First Temple,
phrases.notes: The two vessels are the copper cymbal and the copper mortar from the last two steps.

phrases.english: and they got damaged, and there was no repair for them,
and about them David said:
"burnished copper," "polished copper,"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 7:45 and דברי הימים ב 4:16.

phrases.english: and about them the verse says:
"And vessels of fine golden copper, two, precious as gold."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ שְׁנֵי כֵלִים נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ מִמִּקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from steps 22-24 by naming the origin of the cymbal and mortar and linking them to פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cymbal and mortar were irreplaceable copper vessels from the מקדש ראשון, described in פסוקים as finely polished copper precious as gold.

steps.title: How valuable were the copper vessels compared to gold?
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל disagree about the meaning of 'two, precious as gold.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל disagree. One says each copper vessel was worth as much as two gold vessels. The other says the two copper vessels together were worth one gold vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement between רב and שמואל about how to read the words 'two, precious as gold' from the פסוק in עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'two' and 'precious as gold' can be read two ways. One view: each vessel alone equals two gold vessels, so this copper was worth even more than gold. The other view: both vessels together equal one gold vessel, so they were very valuable for copper but still worth less than gold.

keyTerms.meaning: equal in value, worth the same as

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say which opinion belongs to רב and which to שמואל. It just says 'one said... and one said...'

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel: one said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד שָׁקוּל כִּשְׁנַיִם שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: each and every one was worth as much as two of gold,
and one said:
the two of them together were worth as much as one of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words 'two, precious as gold' from the פסוק quoted in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two readings: each copper vessel equaled two gold vessels, or both together equaled one gold vessel.

steps.title: A teaching of רב יוסף matches the second view
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches a ברייתא that says both vessels together were worth one of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: both of them together were worth as much as one of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching from רב יוסף that agrees with the second opinion in the argument between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's teaching uses the exact words of the second view. That gives that reading support from an older source, though the גמרא does not reject the first view outright.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
the two of them together were worth as much as one of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives older support to the second opinion in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The view that both copper vessels together were worth one gold vessel.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רב יוסף with the same wording.

steps.title: רבי נתן: there were pairs of each vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן reads 'two' (שנים) as 'pairs' (שניים), so there were two cymbals and two mortars.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: they came in pairs, because the פסוק says 'two.' Don't read it as 'two' but as 'pairs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different way to read the word 'two' in the פסוק from עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל used the word 'two' to compare the value of copper and gold. רבי נתן reads the same word with slightly different vowels, so it means 'pairs.' He means each kind of vessel came in a set of two.

keyTerms.meaning: don't read it as... but as... (reading a word with different vowels to learn something extra)

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
they were pairs, as it says: "two";
do not read "two," but "pairs."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the word 'two' from the one used by רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vessels came in pairs: two cymbals and two mortars.

steps.title: Widening the שילוח spring made its water shrink
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells how the king widened the שילוח opening to get more water, but it gave less, until they made it small again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שילוח spring used to pour out water through an opening the size of an איסר coin. The king ordered them to widen it so more water would come, but the water got less. They made it small again, and the water flowed as before. This fulfills the פסוק: 'Let the wise man not brag about his wisdom, and let the strong man not brag about his strength.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another story with the same lesson as the ברייתא about the מקדש vessels: a human 'improvement' made things worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the gold-plated flute and the repaired cymbal and mortar, the king's plan backfired. Only returning the spring to its original size brought the water back. The פסוק from ירמיהו teaches that human cleverness and power cannot control everything.

keyTerms.meaning: the Siloam spring or pool in ירושלים
a small coin, used here to describe the size of the opening

steps.whatToRemember: All these stories teach the same thing: the old vessels and the שילוח worked best as they were, and human 'improvements' only spoiled them.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught:
the Shiloach used to pour out water through an opening the size of an issar coin;
the king gave an order, and they widened it
so that its water would increase, but it decreased;
so they went back and made it smaller, and it poured out water again,
to fulfill what is said:
"Let the wise man not brag about his wisdom,
and let the strong man not brag about his strength."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new story with the same theme as the ברייתא in steps 22-25: human changes spoiled something that worked well as it was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Widening the שילוח reduced its water, and making it small again restored it, showing that human wisdom and power have limits.

steps.title: There was no הרדולים in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches that there was no instrument called a הרדולים in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise רבן שמעון בן גמליאל used to say: There was no הרדולים in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, this time about a musical instrument that was not used in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'likewise' marks this as another teaching from the same רבן שמעון בן גמליאל who taught about the שילוח in step 29. This time the topic is a musical instrument that was not used in the מקדש. The reason comes in step 32.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain musical instrument. The גמרא explains it next.
And likewise. It links this teaching to the one before it.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And likewise Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel would say:
There was no hirdolim in the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second teaching from the same תנא, connected by 'likewise' to his story about the שילוח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הרדולים instrument was not used in the מקדש.

steps.title: What is a הרדולים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word הרדולים means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a הרדולים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what this unfamiliar word means. This question sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot understand why the instrument was left out until we know what it is. So the גמרא first defines the term.

keyTerms.meaning: What is. Used to ask for the meaning of a word.

phrases.english: What is a hirdolim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word used in Step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the instrument called הרדולים.

steps.title: אביי explains: a water organ that ruins the melody
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a הרדולים is a water organ. It was not used because its sound is pleasant but it mixes up the melody.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a water organ. It was not used because its sound is pleasant, but it mixes up the melody.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. He identifies the instrument and explains why it was kept out of the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was not that the instrument sounded bad. Its sound was pleasant, but it mixed up the melody. So a pleasant sound alone was not enough to bring an instrument into the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A water organ, an instrument powered by water.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the instrument was rejected because it sounded bad. Its sound was pleasant, but it disturbed the melody.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is a hydraulic organ,
because its sound is pleasant
but it disrupts the melody.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 31 and gives the reason for the rule in Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הרדולים is a water organ. It was excluded because its pleasant sound disrupted the melody.

steps.title: There was a מגריפה in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, quoted through רב מתנה and רבא בר שילא, teaches that there was an instrument called a מגריפה in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר שילא said in the name of רב מתנה, who said in the name of שמואל: There was a מגריפה in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about another instrument, one that was used in the מקדש. The description of it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After an instrument that was not in the מקדש, the גמרא now turns to one that was. The details of what the מגריפה was and how it sounded come next.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of an instrument in the מקדש. The גמרא describes it next.

phrases.english: Rava bar Sheila said
that Rav Mattana said that Shmuel said:
There was a magreifa in the Temple,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from an instrument that was not in the מקדש to one that was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An instrument called the מגריפה was present in the מקדש.
